reviews.title: App Should Be Renamed Spamr
reviews.text:
Despite charging more than $70 a year for service, the app developers can’t seem to prevent annoying spam and bot accounts from being created. Additionally, the UI is among the worst out there, with extremely inefficient use of screen real estate, convoluted access to features, and an outdated design and color scheme. It seems the vast majority of resources are dedicated to the livestream feature with its dizzying array of for purchase animations and confusing controls. Too bad the developers don’t spend more time on the fundamentals of what makes a good app instead of milking this digital cash cow for all it’s worth.

Now that it’s been bought by the owners of Scruff, a minor UI update has been rolled out which has made the UI even worse than before. Tap on a profile and the top quarter of the main photo is obscured by an opaque strip with a cartoonish back button on the left and a caution icon on the right. You have to tap again to see the full image. Despite the change in ownership, Growlr remains a very poorly designed, bot plagued, overpriced hookup app that allows actual women and men pretending to be women to join. Pathetic.

reviews.title: Terrible user experience
reviews.text:
Registration process is moronic and agains any standard practice of checking if you have correct email or password. It uses single entry “box”, so if you accidentally made mistake you would never know. For some reason password suggested and stored by “passwords” app do not work( details captured during registration do not match login process later on). So if you log off from the app you won’t be able to log in unless you magically remembered the random generated passwords. “Forgot password “ option doesn’t work. Email with reset link is never sent. Not to inbox not to spam. Contacting support resulted in template pointless instructions that didn’t worked in the first place.

UPDATE:

The messaging system has a long-standing design flaw. Messages are deleted from the server within minutes and only live on the devices, which is fine for privacy in an app like this. But the delivery layer is unreliable — users routinely get notifications with no message appearing, or have to restart the app/device just to see chats.
Support replies under reviews almost always just say “contact us with your device, OS and app version” instead of acknowledging this is a systemic server-side limitation that has been reported for years. Fix the delivery reliability and badge/inbox sync. The local-storage approach is understandable; the constant glitches are not.

reviews.title: Banned for no reason
reviews.text:
I’ve been a paying subscriber for years and have regularly used the livestream feature without issue. Recently, my stream was abruptly terminated for allegedly violating the Code of Conduct. The content in question showed nothing more than a bare male chest — the same chest that has been accepted daily for years-no nudity, no explicit activity, and nothing outside what is commonplace on this platform.

After reviewing the published rules carefully, I cannot see how any violation occurred. What is more concerning is the complete lack of response from support despite multiple emails requesting clarification.

If moderation policies have changed, they should be clearly stated and applied consistently. As it stands, enforcement appears arbitrary and opaque, and paying subscribers are left without explanation.

Until Growlr provides clearer guidelines and responsive support, I cannot recommend the app.
